target.title: feat: block broad protected-root shell searches
target.body:
Closes #99466
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex/OpenClaw workers could run broad recursive shell searches over high-risk roots such as a home directory, Codex/OpenClaw state, session archives, repo parents, or external workspace roots. On small PR tasks this can turn command output and local session/debug surfaces into oversized live context, making runaway token usage much more likely.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a high-confidence exec guard for `rg`, recursive `grep`, and `find` commands in gateway/sandbox execution. The guard reuses OpenClaw's existing command-payload analysis so shell wrappers and command carriers are inspected, blocks only protected-root search shapes, and returns actionable guidance to narrow the path, prefer indexed/search tools, and cap output.

This first pass does not add a user-configurable bypass. It is intentionally scoped to the riskiest broad search shapes from the worker-runaway retro and keeps narrowed repo/task/evidence-path searches allowed.

## User Impact

Agents get an immediate, actionable exec failure instead of walking large protected roots. Narrow searches inside a repo or task directory continue to work, and the exec tool description now teaches the safer default before the command is attempted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts`: 8 passed
  - `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts`: 43 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`
  - 53 passed
- `git diff --check`

Public issue/PR artifacts intentionally avoid raw private transcripts, cookies, endpoint secrets, and full local session logs.

## Mergeability Proof Update (2026-07-04)

Redacted behavior proof for ClawSweeper, from PR head `29aef945f023cb2a5ebbe7b9170d799f2386c7c2`:

- Fixed ClawSweeper P2: subshell `cd` no longer leaks into later outer commands; cwd tracking is scoped by enclosing shell parentheses.
- Fixed CI failure in `checks-node-compact-large-whole-1`: exact deferred-followup guidance tests now include the new search-safety sentence in the exec tool description.
- Runtime guard proof, using the same pre-exec guard called by gateway/sandbox execution and without running any filesystem search:
  - `rg timeout` from `<HOME>`: blocked over protected root `<HOME>`.
  - `find src -name '*.ts'` from `/Volumes/LEXAR/repos/openclaw`: allowed as a narrowed repo search.
  - `(cd ~/.codex/sessions); rg timeout` from `/Volumes/LEXAR/repos/openclaw`: allowed because the later `rg` runs in the outer repo cwd.
  - `(cd ~/.codex/sessions; rg timeout)` from `/Volumes/LEXAR/repos/openclaw`: blocked over protected root `<HOME>/.codex/sessions`.
- Regression proof: `does not leak subshell cd into later outer commands` and `keeps subshell cd scoped to commands inside the same subshell` were added.
- Focused validation run after the latest fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts` passed, 3 tests.
- Focused validation run after the latest fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts` passed, 24 tests.
- Focused validation run after the latest fix: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` passed, 96 tests.
- Focused validation run after the latest fix: `git diff --check && node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.ts src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts src/agents/bash-tools.descriptions.ts src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts` passed.
- Policy boundary: v1 intentionally keeps a fail-closed/no-bypass default for high-confidence protected-root searches; an audited bypass can be discussed as a follow-up if maintainers want one.



## Mergeability Proof Update (2026-07-04, head 937302b1b0)

- Fixed current P2 review: `cd` cwd tracking now only adopts a target directory when it resolves with `realpath`; failed `cd /definitely-missing...; rg token` preserves the original protected cwd and blocks broad search. Regression: `preserves cwd when a failed cd would leave the shell in place`.
- Fixed current P2 review: GitHub runner-style workspace parents such as `/home/runner/work/openclaw` are protected when a job runs inside `/home/runner/work/openclaw/openclaw` and searches `..`. Regression: `blocks searches over GitHub runner-style repo parents`.
- Existing subshell cwd regressions were kept machine-independent by creating a temporary synthetic `~/.codex/sessions` path, so CI no longer depends on local session directories existing.
- Runtime guard proof after these fixes, without running any filesystem search: `failed-cd-from-home` blocked over `<HOME>`; `runner-parent-rg` blocked over `<RUNNER_HOME>/work/openclaw`; narrowed repo `find src -name "*.ts"` remained allowed.
- Focused validation after these fixes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts` passed, 26 tests.
- Focused validation after these fixes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` passed, 96 tests.
- Focused validation after these fixes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts` passed, 3 tests.
- Focused validation after these fixes: `git diff --check && node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.ts src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts src/agents/bash-tools.descriptions.ts src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts` passed.



## Mergeability Proof Update (2026-07-04, head 510ed9485d)

- Fixed current P2 review: shell `cd` no longer mutates tracked cwd when the parsed command is inside an `if ... then ... fi` body that may not execute. Regression: `does not apply cd from an unexecuted control-flow branch`.
- Fixed current P2 review: `rg -E` is now treated as a value-taking encoding option. Regression coverage is in `skips rg value operands before inferring implicit cwd searches`.
- Fixed current P2 review: `find --` now skips the option terminator before collecting path operands. Regression: `skips find option terminators before path operands`.
- Fixed current P2 review: sandbox broad-search checks now resolve against the sandbox container cwd, not only the host mirror path. Regression: `checks sandbox broad searches against the container cwd`.
- Fixed current P2 review: shell `~` expands against OS shell home even when `OPENCLAW_HOME` differs. Regression: `expands shell tilde against OS home instead of OPENCLAW_HOME`.
- Fixed current P2 review: `env -C` / `--chdir` cwd is preserved while unwrapping command carriers. Regression: `preserves env --chdir cwd when unwrapping command carriers`.
- Fixed current P2 review: descendants of protected Codex/OpenClaw state roots are blocked, with deepest-root diagnostics. Regression: `blocks descendants of protected state roots`.
- Fixed current P2 review: shell positional dispatch wrappers using `$@` / `$*` are analyzed. Regression: `resolves shell positional dispatch wrappers`.
- Fixed current P2 review: pathless `rg` in a pipeline is treated as stdin filtering, not an implicit filesystem search. Regression: `does not treat piped rg filters as filesystem searches`.
- Focused validation after these fixes: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-control-command-guard.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.deferred-followup-guidance.test.ts` passed, 33 + 97 + 3 tests.

target.title: Persist gateway restart audit events
target.body:
## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. That leaves avoidable ambiguity between internal restart requests and external/manual signals.

This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. The audit captures reason/source/session metadata plus safe-restart preflight context so future incidents can be attributed directly from state/log evidence.

target.title: improve: enforce canonical QA scenario ownership
target.body:
Closes #99627

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a QA maintenance problem where scenario IDs could be owned by both the canonical YAML inventory and a code-defined live transport catalog without one validation failure identifying both owners. It also prevents helper-level or in-memory tests from being presented as primary evidence for coverage that requires a real product boundary executable.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `qa coverage` path now records one owner for every YAML flow, script, Vitest, and Playwright scenario plus every remaining Discord, Slack, Telegram, and WhatsApp live scenario. Coverage generation rejects duplicate IDs with both source references, reports the remaining legacy owner count, and keeps helper-backed claims under supporting `coverage.secondary` metadata. The existing live transport CLI commands remain mounted on the shared `openclaw qa` host.

Legacy catalog and compatibility-wrapper deletion criteria are documented so migrations can remove old owners only after canonical YAML execution and evidence parity are established.

## User Impact

There is no end-user runtime behavior change. QA maintainers and contributors get deterministic duplicate-ID failures, explicit ownership in machine-readable coverage output, and more accurate scorecard evidence semantics.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/coverage-report.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-catalog.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/scenario-packs.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/shared/live-transport-scenarios.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/cli.runtime.test.ts` — 223 tests passed.

target.title: fix: keep OpenClaw control tools available when tool_search misroutes
target.body:
Closes #99464
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server workers could be told to discover OpenClaw session/control tools through `tool_search`, but `tool_search` could resolve a different connector universe and leave the worker without the OpenClaw delegation/control tools it needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now keeps the critical control-path dynamic tools, `heartbeat_respond`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`, in the direct Codex tool surface while leaving broad OpenClaw tools deferred/searchable. This preserves Codex-native `spawn_agent` as the recommended Codex-subagent path in developer instructions, but removes the unsafe dependency on a successful deferred search result for OpenClaw/ACP delegation and heartbeat handling.

Codex source inspection for this change used sibling `../codex` at `da4c8ca57d40b074bdc1b5b1218851100150c56b`:

- `codex-rs/app-server/README.md:1557-1566` documents that deferred dynamic functions must be namespaced and are searchable only when `tool_search` is available.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:494-536` enables deferred-tool guidance only when the search tool is enabled.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:964-984` builds `tool_search` only from planned deferred runtimes with search info.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/tool_search.rs:74-87` builds the search index from the supplied deferred-tool search infos.

## User Impact

OpenClaw Codex workers keep access to OpenClaw heartbeat and session delegation controls even when deferred `tool_search` is unavailable or returns unrelated connector results. Operators should see fewer fallbacks to expensive raw shell inspection when an OpenClaw worker needs OpenClaw-specific session controls.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.test.ts`
  - 81 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
  - 116 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts`

- `git diff --check`
  - Passed.

- Initial grouped local Vitest run was stopped after going quiet for local resource safety; the same target files were then run one at a time and passed.
- No raw private worker transcript or session JSONL content is included in this PR.
- AI-assisted change.

Use tool_search to load exact callable specs before use.`

target.title: fix(watch-node): defer restart when dist/entry.js is missing mid-rebuild
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: When a git pull triggers source file changes while `dist/` is mid-rebuild, the hot-reload watcher (`watch-node.mjs`) kills the current healthy gateway process and restarts into a missing `dist/entry.js`, causing an 8x crash-loop that exhausts systemd's restart limit.

**Solution**: Check build readiness before restarting. The new `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs)` function verifies that both `dist/entry.js` exists AND the build stamp's git HEAD matches the current checkout HEAD. If either check fails (missing entry, mismatched HEAD, missing stamp, or stamp without HEAD), the restart is deferred and polled every 2s until the build is verified fresh. An additional guard in the child-process exit handler prevents crash-looping when the watcher would otherwise restart into a stale build after a child exit.

**What changed**: Two files — `scripts/watch-node.mjs` and `test/scripts/watch-node.test.ts`.

**What did NOT change**: Build logic (`tsdown-build.mjs`), source watch paths, the `dist/` IGNORE segment, or `run-node.mjs`.

Fixes #99603

## What Problem This Solves

Production gateway deployments using a git checkout with hot-reload (via systemd) are vulnerable to a crash-loop when a `git pull` triggers a rebuild while `dist/` is mid-build. The watcher kills the currently-healthy gateway and restarts into a missing entrypoint. This caused a 37-minute production outage on 2026-07-03.

## Root Cause

`watch-node.mjs:requestRestart()` unconditionally sends SIGTERM to the healthy gateway child process whenever chokidar detects a relevant source file change (e.g. from `git pull`). During a rebuild, `tsdown-build.mjs` calls `cleanTsdownOutputRoots()` which removes `dist/entry.js`. The new child then crashes because the entrypoint doesn't exist, and `shouldRestartAfterChildExit()` treats SIGTERM/exit code 143 as restartable — forming a crash-loop.

**Additionally**: Even when an old `dist/entry.js` exists, the current git HEAD may have changed (after `git pull`), meaning `run-node` will rebuild and clean `dist` after the stop. The old entrypoint check alone is insufficient to prevent the crash-loop.

## Changes

`scripts/watch-node.mjs` (+86 / -37 lines):

### Layer 1 — `isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs, resolveHead)`

Replaces the previous `isDistEntryFresh()` mtime check with a comprehensive build-readiness check:
- Verifies `dist/entry.js` exists (basic guard for mid-rebuild window)
- Reads the `.buildstamp` file from `dist/` and compares its recorded `head` against the current checkout HEAD via `resolveGitHead()`
- If HEADs differ, or if the stamp lacks a `head` but the current HEAD is known, the build is stale — restart is deferred
- Falls back gracefully (entry-only check) when git or stamp file is unavailable

### Layer 2 — Deferred polling (existing, retained)

When build is not ready, polls every 2s instead of dropping the restart request. When the build completes (entry.js + matching stamp appear), auto-triggers the restart.

### Layer 3 — Exit handler guard

On child-process exit (SIGTERM/143), verifies build readiness before restarting. Prevents self-reinforcing crash-loop when the child exits during a rebuild window.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: The hot-reload watcher no longer kills the current healthy gateway child process when the build output is missing or stale for the current checkout.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node v22 — L2 evidence via direct function call with real `fs` module and real `resolveGitHead()` against the worktree git checkout.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```terminal
node evidence-collection.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:

```terminal
======================================================================
L2 Evidence: isBuildReadyForRestart with real fs/git
======================================================================

1. Current git HEAD: 0aeb43d2cc69...

--- Scenario A: Missing dist/entry.js ---
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = false (expected: false)

--- Scenario B: entry.js + matching build stamp ---
   Created: dist/.buildstamp with head: 0aeb43d2cc69...
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = true (expected: true)

--- Scenario C: entry.js + MISMATCHED build stamp ---
   Updated: dist/.buildstamp with head: 00000000... (mismatched)
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = false (expected: false)

--- Scenario D: entry.js exists, NO build stamp ---
   Removed: dist/.buildstamp
   isBuildReadyForRestart(cwd, fs) = false (expected: false)
======================================================================
```

**Observed result after the fix**: `isBuildReadyForRestart` returns `true` only when entry.js exists AND the build stamp HEAD matches the current checkout HEAD. Scenario C directly demonstrates the fix for the review finding: even when an old `dist/entry.js` exists (simulating a `git pull` that changed the checkout), a mismatched git HEAD causes the restart to be deferred, preventing the crash-loop. 17/17 unit tests pass covering all code paths.

**What was not tested**: Real Gateway integration with live systemd restart race (requires controlled git-pull-triggered rebuild environment). The pure-function and exit-handler tests provide L2 coverage for all code paths.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Claude Sonnet 5 (`claude-sonnet-5`, released 2026-06-30) ships from Anthropic with a 1,000,000-token context window. OpenClaw 2026.6.11's bundled Anthropic plugin catalog has no entry for it, and the model is also missing from `ANTHROPIC_GA_1M_MODEL_PREFIXES` (duplicated in `context-resolution.ts` and `stream-wrappers.ts`).

Users who add `claude-sonnet-5` as a custom model (with `contextWindow: 1000000`) still see the model treated as 200k-context wherever the bundled static catalog or GA-1M prefix check is consulted.

Fixes #99239

## Why This Change Was Made

Three locations needed updates:

1. **`extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.json`** — add model to both `claude-cli` and `anthropic` provider lists with correct `contextWindow` and `maxTokens`:
   - Claude CLI: `contextWindow: 1048576`, `maxTokens: 128000` (consistent with claude-opus-4-8)
   - Anthropic: `contextWindow: 1000000`, `maxTokens: 128000` (consistent with claude-fable-5)

2. **`src/agents/context-resolution.ts`** — add `claude-sonnet-5` / `claude-sonnet-5.0` to `ANTHROPIC_GA_1M_MODEL_PREFIXES` so `resolveAnthropicFixedContextWindow()` recognizes it

3. **`extensions/anthropic/stream-wrappers.ts`** — add same prefixes to the duplicated constant so `isAnthropic1MModel()` treats it as GA-1M (skips legacy beta header)

## Evidence

### Tests

```
✓ extension-anthropic stream-wrappers.test.ts (21 tests)
✓ extension-anthropic openclaw.plugin.test.ts (1 test)
```

### Before vs After (sanity check)

**Before**: claude-sonnet-5 is NOT a GA-1M model prefix
```
$ node -e "
const prefixes = ['claude-opus-4-8','claude-opus-4.8','claude-opus-4-6','claude-opus-4.6','claude-opus-4-7','claude-opus-4.7','claude-sonnet-4-6','claude-sonnet-4.6'];
console.log('sonnet-5 is GA-1M:', prefixes.some(p => 'claude-sonnet-5'.startsWith(p)));
"
// sonnet-5 is GA-1M: false
```

**After**: claude-sonnet-5 is recognized as GA-1M
```
// sonnet-5 is GA-1M: true
```

### Plugin JSON validation

```bash
$ node -e "const p = require('./extensions/anthropic/openclaw.plugin.json');
const cliCL = p.modelCatalog.providers['claude-cli'].models.find(m => m.id === 'claude-sonnet-5');
const anth = p.modelCatalog.providers.anthropic.models.find(m => m.id === 'claude-sonnet-5');
console.log('claude-cli:', cliCL?.contextWindow, cliCL?.maxTokens);
console.log('anthropic:', anth?.contextWindow, anth?.maxTokens);"
// claude-cli: 1048576 128000
// anthropic: 1000000 128000
```

## Merge Risk

Low. This is a static catalog addition. The GA-1M prefix entry enables 1M-context semantics for the model, replacing the 200k fallback. No functional changes to existing models.

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): resolve 200K context window for Claude 3.x and unlisted Anthropic Bedrock variants
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` only listed a handful of Anthropic models in `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS`. Common Bedrock IDs such as `anthropic.claude-3-opus-20240229-v1:0`, `anthropic.claude-3-sonnet-20240229-v1:0`, and `anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-2024{0620,1022}-v{1,2}:0` fell through to `defaults.contextWindow` (32K by default), so prompts well below the model's actual 200K window tripped context-overflow precheck and triggered auto-compaction restart loops.
- Why it matters: every Bedrock customer using a Claude 3.x base model that wasn't already enumerated saw the gateway's in-memory model registry advertise 32K and refuse prompts the model could otherwise serve.
- What changed: backfill the missing Claude 3 / 3.5 / Opus 4 base entries at 200K, then add a small `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FAMILIES` table with an `^anthropic\.claude-(3|4)` regex so unlisted future variants and region-prefixed inference profiles (`us.anthropic.claude-*`, `jp.anthropic.claude-*`, etc.) default to 200K. Explicit table entries still win for higher-tier (1M) Claude rows.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no other vendor families. The `defaultContextWindow` config knob is untouched. Inference-profile prefix stripping logic and existing strict matches are unchanged.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix

## Scope

- [x] amazon-bedrock plugin (provider discovery)

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #73328
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

- Root cause: `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` was a hand-maintained map and missed the Claude 3 / 3.5 base IDs that most users encounter on Bedrock. There was no family-level fallback, so any unmatched model fell through to `resolveDefaultContextWindow` (32K default).
- Missing detection / guardrail: no test verified the family-level resolution; existing tests only cover Claude 3.7 / 4.x rows that happened to be in the map.
- Contributing context: AWS does not expose token-limit metadata via `ListFoundationModelsCommand`, so any unmatched model gets the conservative default.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`
- Scenarios the test locks in:
  - Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2 (`anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022-v2:0`) resolves to 200K via the explicit table entry.
  - An unlisted future Claude 3 variant (`anthropic.claude-3-future-preview-v9:0`) resolves to 200K via the `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOW_FAMILIES` fallback rather than 32K.
  - The same family fallback works for region-prefixed inference profiles (`us.anthropic.claude-3-future-preview-v9:0`).
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the bug surface is "missing entry / no fallback in `resolveKnownContextWindow`". The new tests pin both the table backfill and the family fallback, including the inference-profile prefix path.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Bedrock-discovered Claude 3.x models now report 200K context windows in the gateway's in-memory model registry instead of 32K.
- Bedrock-discovered Anthropic models with IDs not listed in `KNOWN_CONTEXT_WINDOWS` default to 200K via family fallback instead of 32K.
- No other providers are affected.

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Steps

1. Configure a Bedrock provider with default discovery and a Claude 3.5 Sonnet (or any unlisted Claude 3.x) model.
2. Boot the gateway and inspect the in-memory model registry / `/health/deep`.
3. Send a prompt totalling ~16K input tokens.

### Expected

- `contextWindow` reported as 200000 for `anthropic.claude-*` Bedrock models, no context-overflow precheck triggered for the 16K prompt.

### Actual (before fix)

- `contextWindow=32000`; the 16K prompt is treated as nearly full and triggers `[context-overflow-precheck] estimatedPromptTokens=16300 promptBudgetBeforeReserve=15616` → `Auto-compaction failed.*Restarting session`.

## Evidence

- Static reproduction is provided by the new unit tests in `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.test.ts`. Live Bedrock validation requires AWS credentials and is left to CI / downstream verification.

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: TypeScript clean on touched files; new tests added next to existing `discovery.test.ts` Claude/Sonnet suite.
- Edge cases checked: explicit table entries still win (e.g. Claude Sonnet 4.6 @ 1M), region-prefixed inference profiles route through stripping then family fallback, non-Claude families (Llama, Mistral, etc.) untouched.
- What I did NOT verify: a live Bedrock call with AWS credentials; full `pnpm check` / `pnpm test` was not exercised locally, leaving CI as the verification surface.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes — existing explicit table entries are unchanged. Only previously-incorrect 32K resolutions become 200K.
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a non-Anthropic Bedrock model id happens to start with `anthropic.claude-3` or `anthropic.claude-4`.
  - Mitigation: AWS's Bedrock model id namespace is provider-prefixed (`anthropic.`), so this regex is well-scoped to the Claude family. The explicit map still takes precedence and any future tier-bump (e.g. another 1M variant) just needs another explicit entry.

AI-assisted: yes (Codex).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users selecting `/think max` or `/think xhigh` with `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-pro` or `opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash` would have the requested thinking level silently clamped down before the OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 request was built.

The OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 model rows now carry an explicit thinking-level map in both runtime catalog data and manifest metadata: `off` disables thinking, normal levels map to DeepSeek's low/medium/high efforts, and `xhigh`/`max` map to DeepSeek's max effort. The fix stays inside the opencode-go provider metadata so the existing generic clamp and DeepSeek V4 OpenAI-compatible stream wrapper continue to own their current behavior.

## User Impact

OpenCode Go DeepSeek V4 users can use max/xhigh thinking and have the request reach the provider as max effort instead of being downgraded to high. Static model discovery and runtime provider discovery now agree on the same DeepSeek V4 thinking capabilities.

target.title: feat(exec): inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID env vars for child processes
target.body:
## Summary
Inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` environment variables into child processes spawned by the exec tool, allowing scripts and skills to reliably identify the current session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

Supersedes #68859 with full coverage including node-host execution, regression tests, and docs updates.

Closes #66705

## Problem
Currently, skills and scripts executed via exec have no reliable way to determine which session or agent they belong to. While the model can pass these identifiers as parameters, this approach is prone to hallucination errors where the model may provide incorrect values.

This blocks workflows where a child process needs to register a callback or webhook that routes back to the originating session.

## Solution
Automatically inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` into the environment of child processes spawned by exec, across all execution paths.

### Changes

**Core injection:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` — inject both vars in `runExecProcess` (`shellRuntimeEnv`)
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` — inject both vars in `shellRuntimeEnv` after sanitization for `host=node` execution
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts` — pass `agentId` through gateway allowlist path

**Type updates:**
- Added `agentId?: string` to `runExecProcess` opts type

**Documentation:**
- `docs/help/environment.md` — document both new env vars
- `docs/tools/exec.md` — note session/agent injection for all exec hosts

**Tests:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts` — 6 new tests covering gateway injection, user env override prevention, and empty-string clearing semantics
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — updated sanitizer allowlist test to verify trusted var injection
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` — removed stale test (gateway no longer injects vars into `requestedEnv`)

## Testing
- [x] Local gateway execution (host=gateway)
- [x] Sandbox execution (host=sandbox) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] PTY mode (pty=true) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] Node-host execution (host=node) — unit tests in invoke-system-run.test.ts
- [x] Override semantics — user env cannot override trusted values
- [x] Clearing semantics — empty string when no agent/session defaults provided

## Usage Example
```python
import os
session_key = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY")
agent_id = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID")
```

## Backward Compatibility
Fully backward compatible:
- Variables always set (empty string when not available), avoiding stale-value issues
- Trusted values override any user-provided env overrides with the same names
- No existing behavior changed

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID environment variables into exec child processes so skills and scripts can reliably identify their session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw 2026.4.2, macOS arm64, gateway mode

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Built and ran OpenClaw gateway with the patched code
2. Created a minimal test skill at workspace/skills/test-env-injection/ that prints both environment variables
3. Executed the skill script via the exec tool within a main agent session
4. Captured the console output

**Evidence after fix**:
```bash
$ python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/test-env-injection/test.py
agent:main:2
main
```

**Observed result after fix**: Both OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID are correctly injected into the exec child process environment. The output matches the expected session key (agent:main:2) and agent id (main).

**What was not tested**: Node-host (host=node) execution path was not tested in a real multi-node setup; only unit tests cover this path.

target.title: fix(exec-policy): accept trusted ~/.openclaw symlink at home boundary
target.body:
Fixes #72572.

## Problem

The exec-approvals symlink hardening from #72377 only relaxed the restriction on the `OPENCLAW_HOME` root itself, so a symlinked `~/.openclaw` immediate child of a real home directory still trips `assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()`:

\`\`\`
Refusing to traverse symlink in exec approvals path: /Users/funjim/.openclaw
\`\`\`

This breaks \`openclaw exec-policy preset yolo\` (and every other exec-policy command) for users who manage their OpenClaw config via GNU Stow, chezmoi, or any other dotfile-managed setup that exposes \`~/.openclaw → ~/dotfiles/openclaw/.openclaw\`.

## Fix

Allow EXACTLY ONE trusted symlink hop at the immediate child of the trusted home root, gated by the same hardening intent as #64050 / #72377:

1. Only the immediate child of the trusted root may be a symlink (deeper symlinks inside the resolved tree remain rejected).
2. The symlink target's realpath must be owned by the current effective user (\`process.geteuid()\`).
3. The symlink target must not be group- or other-writable (mode bits \`0o022\`).
4. After consuming the trusted hop, traversal continues from the realpath target with the original per-segment symlink rejection — a second symlink anywhere below is still rejected.

Permissive on platforms without \`process.geteuid\` (Windows), where the OS ACL model already differs.

\`ensureDir()\` is taught to accept a \`dir\` whose \`lstatSync\` reports a symlink, but only after re-asserting the realpath target is a directory — \`assertNoSymlinkPathComponents()\` already vetted ownership/perms.

## Tests

- **New**: \`accepts a symlinked ~/.openclaw immediate child of the trusted home\` — constructs the exact GNU Stow layout from the issue and verifies the file lands at the realpath target.
- **Updated**: \`refuses to traverse symlinked approvals components below a symlinked home\` — now constructs an unsafe (group-writable) symlink target so the deeper-symlink rejection intent of #72377 is still exercised. The original test became implicitly the same scenario as the new accept-test once the trusted-hop relaxation landed; making the target unsafe keeps the rejection branch under test.

All 18 \`exec-approvals-store\` tests pass; \`pnpm tsgo:test\` clean.

## Diff

+92 / -3 across 2 production files + 1 test file + CHANGELOG.

## Refs

- Original hardening: #64050
- Replaced PR (broader fix): #64663
- Merged narrow replacement: #72377
- This PR strictly broadens #72377 in the safe direction the issue describes.

target.title: fix(mcp): reject mixed command+url transport config (#72111)
target.body:
Closes #72111.

## Problem

When an MCP server config carries **both** a non-empty `command` and a non-empty `url` (e.g. a streamable-http endpoint plus a `command`/`args` pair), the runtime silently picks stdio and drops the HTTP transport. The user sees:

```
MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms
```

The spawned child never speaks JSON-RPC over stdio because the user actually wanted the streamable-http endpoint. The clawsweeper bot triaged this and recommended early rejection over silent fallback.

## Root cause

`resolveMcpTransportConfig` in `src/agents/mcp-transport-config.ts` resolves the stdio launch first when `command` is set, regardless of whether `url` is also set. The 30s timeout that follows is the user-visible symptom; the silent fallback at config-resolution time is the real bug.

## Reproducer

In `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  \"mcp\": {
    \"servers\": {
      \"broken\": {
        \"command\": \"node\",
        \"args\": [\"something.js\"],
        \"url\": \"https://my-mcp.example.com/mcp\"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Run OpenClaw → the `broken` server hangs, then errors with `MCP server connection timed out after 30000ms`. There is no clue in the logs about *which* transport was actually attempted.

## Fix

Reject the ambiguous shape early with a clear diagnostic that names the offending server and the requested transport hint, matching the file's existing \"skipped server X because Y\" diagnostic style and the clawsweeper bot's \"Best possible solution\":

> reject mixed `command` + `url`/HTTP transport configs early with a clear diagnostic and docs/test alignment. The current silent stdio precedence should not remain the user-visible timeout path.

Implementation: when `command` and a non-whitespace `url` are both present, log the warning, return `null` (caller already handles `null` as \"skip this server\"), and let the user fix their config.

Pure stdio configs (no `url`) and pure HTTP configs (no `command`) are unaffected. **Whitespace-only `url`** strings continue to be treated as \"no url\" so stdio still wins, matching the existing trimming in `mcp-stdio.ts`.

Diff: **+17** lines in `mcp-transport-config.ts`, **+52** in tests.

## Verification

```
pnpm vitest run src/agents/mcp-transport-config.test.ts
# 11 passed (7 original + 4 new)

pnpm check
# 0 errors, 0 warnings; all policy guards green
```

## Tests added (4 new)

1. **Mixed config + transport hint** → resolution returns `null`; warning lists both `command` and `url` and the requested transport.
2. **Mixed config without explicit transport hint** → still rejected; warning is informative.
3. **Whitespace-only `url` paired with real `command`** → resolution returns stdio (mirrors `mcp-stdio.ts` trimming).
4. **Sanitized transport in warning** → diagnostic does not leak full URL secrets / query strings.

## Risk notes

- **Behavior change is user-visible**: configs that used to silently fall back to stdio when both `command`+`url` were set now get rejected outright (server skipped, no spawn). That is the bot-blessed shape and matches the issue, but anyone relying on the silent fallback (unlikely — it was the bug) will see a behavior shift on upgrade.
- Did NOT touch `src/agents/mcp-stdio.ts` even though the bot's evidence cites it; the rejection is cleaner at the transport-config layer where both fields are visible together.
- PR collision check: 8 open MCP-related PRs in the repo (#66542, #69417, #69039, #65574, #62134, #64316, #62160, #60005); none touch `mcp-transport-config.ts` validation logic for the mixed shape. Safe to land independently.

target.title: fix(models): default input=[text,image] for vision-capable explicit-only models
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #71921.

When a user's `openclaw.json` contains a static model catalog for a provider (e.g. `amazon-bedrock`) and an entry omits the `input` field, `mergeProviderModels` previously returned that entry unchanged whenever discovery had no matching model to inherit from. Downstream `modelSupportsImages` (`dist/images-CzeTciMv.js`) reads `model.input?.includes("image") ?? false` — so `input === undefined` is silently treated as **text-only**, permanently breaking image attachments.

The full chain that produces this state in the wild:

1. `extensions/amazon-bedrock/discovery.ts` imports from `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock`. That package is declared in the extension's `package.json` with `stageRuntimeDependencies: true` and is staged into `~/.openclaw/plugin-runtime-deps/.../node_modules/` on first boot after install/upgrade.
2. If OpenClaw resolves the amazon-bedrock catalog **before** runtime-deps staging completes, the import throws, discovery silently catches it, and returns no models.
3. In that empty-discovery state, a **static catalog** gets persisted into the user's `openclaw.json` for `models.providers.amazon-bedrock.models` — entries carrying `id`, `name`, `contextWindow`, `maxTokens`, but no `input`.
4. On subsequent boots, even after `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` is installed and discovery works correctly, the user still carries that frozen static catalog. `mergeProviderModels` preserves each explicit entry verbatim when there's no matching implicit (discovery) entry, so `input` stays `undefined`.
5. User-visible effect: "Model does not support images" on every Bedrock Claude model, permanently, until the user manually edits `openclaw.json` or `~/.openclaw/agents/*/agent/models.json` to add `input: ["text", "image"]`.

## The fix

Teach `mergeProviderModels` to recognize vision-capable model ID patterns (Claude 3.5+/4.x, GPT-4o / 4.1 / 5 / o-series, Gemini 1.5+, Llama 3.2+ / 4.x vision families) and default `input: ["text", "image"]` when the user's explicit entry omits it and discovery has no match. Explicit entries that already specify `input` (including `input: ["text"]` to opt out of vision) are preserved unchanged, as are entries whose IDs don't match a known vision family.

This makes the merge behaviour "fail safe" for modern multimodal model families: if the user's static catalog is stale or incomplete, vision still works out of the box.

## What this does **not** attempt to fix

Three related issues from #71921 that felt out of scope for this PR — happy to follow up separately if maintainers want:

1. **Bundle `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` directly** instead of staging via runtime-deps, to eliminate the first-boot race that seeds the stale static catalog in the first place.
2. **Refresh explicit catalogs when discovery later succeeds**, so stale entries don't linger forever.
3. **Add unknown-field warnings** in `planOpenClawModelsJson` when a static catalog is persisted without `input` for a model the provider could discover dynamically.

## Tests

New file: `src/agents/models-config.merge.explicit-input-default.test.ts`

- ✅ Defaults Claude Opus 4.x explicit-only entries to `[text, image]`
- ✅ Defaults Sonnet 4.x and Haiku 4.x explicit-only entries
- ✅ Defaults GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5+ families
- ✅ Preserves explicit `input: ["text"]` opt-out overrides
- ✅ Leaves non-vision / pre-vision model families (Titan embeddings, Claude 2, custom text-only) with `input` undefined
- ✅ Still inherits from implicit discovery when both catalogs contain the same model ID

All 6 tests pass locally. Existing `model-catalog.test.ts` and `models-config.*.test.ts` pass without regression.

## Reproduction / user workaround

Workaround for users hitting this before the fix ships:

```bash
python3 - << 'PY'
import json, pathlib
for p in pathlib.Path.home().glob('.openclaw/agents/*/agent/models.json'):
    d = json.loads(p.read_text())
    for m in d.get('providers',{}).get('amazon-bedrock',{}).get('models', []):
        mid = m.get('id','').lower()
        if any(k in mid for k in ['claude-opus-4','claude-sonnet-4','claude-haiku-4','claude-3-5','claude-3-7']):
            if 'image' not in m.get('input', []):
                m['input'] = ['text','image']
    p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2))

p = pathlib.Path.home() / '.openclaw' / 'openclaw.json'
d = json.loads(p.read_text())
for m in d.get('models',{}).get('providers',{}).get('amazon-bedrock',{}).get('models', []):
    mid = m.get('id','').lower()
    if any(k in mid for k in ['claude-opus-4','claude-sonnet-4','claude-haiku-4','claude-3-5','claude-3-7']):
        if 'image' not in m.get('input', []):
            m['input'] = ['text','image']
p.write_text(json.dumps(d, indent=2))
PY
openclaw gateway restart
```

Tested end-to-end on OpenClaw 2026.4.24 with Claude Opus 4.7 on us-east-1 Bedrock.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bedrock vision-capable models (Claude 3.5+/4.x, etc.) silently lose `input: ["text", "image"]` and downstream `modelSupportsImages` returns `false`, breaking image attachments. Bug from #71921. Reproduces whenever `mergeProviderModels` sees an explicit (static-catalog) entry without `input` and no matching implicit (discovery) entry to inherit from — exactly the state seeded after a first-boot race against `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock` runtime-deps staging.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 25.4.0 arm64 Mac mini, OpenClaw 2026.5.18 (commit 50a2481), Node 25.8.0, Claude Opus 4.7 via Amazon Bedrock `us-east-1` (model id `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7`). Author's actual production OpenClaw install, not a sandbox.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

Step 1 — inspect the merged catalog state on the live install:

```bash
python3 -c "import json,pathlib;d=json.loads((pathlib.Path.home()/'.openclaw'/'openclaw.json').read_text());[print(m['id'],'input=',m.get('input','<<UNDEFINED>>')) for m in d['models']['providers']['amazon-bedrock']['models']]"
```

Step 2 — apply the merged regex from `src/agents/models-config.merge.ts` to 24 model IDs (12 vision-family + 12 substring-trap edge cases the unit tests guard). Full script linked under After-fix evidence.

Step 3 — end-to-end image attachment via Bedrock vision (real network call against `us-east-1`):

```bash
aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model \
  --model-id us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7 \
  --region us-east-1 \
  --body fileb://payload.json \
  --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out \
  /tmp/out.json
```

`payload.json` contains the multimodal message body (image + text content blocks).

**After-fix evidence:**

Live screenshot rendered and analyzed by Bedrock Claude Opus 4.7 in the same conversation:

![Real behavior proof — OpenClaw 2026.5.18, Bedrock Opus 4.7](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/03-real-behavior-proof.png)

Linked terminal artifacts:
- Environment dump: [01-environment.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/01-environment.txt)
- 24-case merge-regex verification (with output): [02-merge-logic-proof.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/02-merge-logic-proof.txt)
- Live `aws bedrock-runtime invoke-model` transcript with token counts: [04-bedrock-vision-live.txt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aaronedell/openclaw/64725aa8f591f1564eea044f0c7027d2bc43e8a9/.pr-proofs/72404/04-bedrock-vision-live.txt)

Live Bedrock Opus 4.7 response (verbatim, from artifact 04):

```
=== Bedrock Claude Opus 4.7 response ===
**H1 title:**
OpenClaw PR #72404 — Real behavior proof

**Italicized note below it:**
Generated 2026-05-20 by Odin agent on Aaron's Mac mini (OpenClaw 2026.5.18, Claude Opus 4.7 via Bedrock us-east-1)

**Green check marks (✅) in the verification table:** 12

stop_reason: end_turn
input_tokens: 2228
output_tokens: 130
```

**Observed result after fix:** All 9 Bedrock Claude vision-family entries in the live `openclaw.json` carry `input=['text','image']` after the merge. The exact `VISION_CAPABLE_ID_PATTERNS` from the merged file produce the right answer for **24/24** real model IDs (12 vision → defaulted, 12 non-vision/edge cases → unchanged). End-to-end image attachment to `us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` via `bedrock-runtime invoke-model` succeeds on the first call: model reads the PNG, quotes the H1 and italicized timestamp verbatim, counts the 12 ✅ checkmarks correctly, exits with `stop_reason: end_turn`, 2228 input tokens / 130 output tokens. Without this patch, `modelSupportsImages` returns `false` for these IDs and the attachment never reaches Bedrock.

**What was not tested:** (1) The first-boot runtime-deps race itself — that's the seeding mechanism described in the Summary and is out-of-scope for this fix (called out explicitly under "What this does not attempt to fix"). (2) Non-Bedrock providers (OpenAI, Gemini, Llama vision); their regex coverage is verified by the new unit tests but no live multimodal call was issued against them in this proof. (3) Re-running discovery to refresh stale explicit entries — also explicitly out-of-scope, listed as follow-up #2.

target.title: fix(whatsapp): support edit and unsend actions
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- WhatsApp message actions could not edit or revoke bot-owned messages.
- The old PR also routed edit/unsend through PN-only JID conversion, which could misroute LID-addressed chats.

Why does this matter now?

- WhatsApp outbound sends already use LID-aware routing. Message mutations need the same routing contract or they can target the wrong chat.

What is the intended outcome?

- Add WhatsApp `edit`, `delete`, and `unsend` actions for bot-owned messages.
- Keep `upload-file` support from current `main` while adding the new gateway actions.
- Use `resolveOutboundJid` for edit/unsend so message keys use the resolved LID JID when available.
- Validate edit text before forwarding the gateway action.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- Editing or deleting other users' WhatsApp messages.
- Live WhatsApp server compatibility guarantees beyond Baileys payload construction.

What does success look like?

- `edit` sends a Baileys `{ edit }` payload with `fromMe: true`.
- `delete` and `unsend` send a Baileys `{ delete }` payload with `fromMe: true`.
- PN-to-LID mappings are honored for normal sends, reactions, edit, unsend, and typing presence.

What should reviewers focus on?

- LID-aware routing in `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.ts`.
- Gateway action dispatch in `extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.ts`.
- `actions.sendMessage` gating and target authorization in `extensions/whatsapp/src/action-runtime.ts`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #14344

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #67378

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

- This refresh addresses the existing PR review blocker about reusing LID-aware routing for edit and unsend.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: WhatsApp edit/unsend now use the same LID-aware outbound JID resolution as normal sends and reactions.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on Linux with Node/pnpm and the real WhatsApp send API seam; temp Baileys auth dir containing `lid-mapping-15555550000.json`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/action-runtime.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-actions.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/send.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/active-listener.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

- Evidence after fix:

```text
✓ createWebSendApi LID resolution (issue #67378) > resolves PN to LID for editMessage
✓ createWebSendApi LID resolution (issue #67378) > resolves PN to LID for unsendMessage
Test Files  7 passed (7)
Tests  144 passed (144)
```

- Observed result after fix: edit and unsend calls send to `987654@lid`; their message keys use `remoteJid: "987654@lid"`, `id: "msg-2"`, and `fromMe: true`.
- What was not tested: live WhatsApp account behavior against WhatsApp servers.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: no linked live WhatsApp account was available in this local repair environment, so the proof covers OpenClaw routing, dispatch, gating, payload construction, log sanitization, and listener contracts, not server acceptance.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): the old edit/unsend implementation called `toWhatsappJid(to)`, so a PN target with a LID mapping stayed on `15555550000@s.whatsapp.net` instead of `987654@lid`.

## Tests and validation

Which commands did you run?

```text
pnpm docs:list
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test extensions/whatsapp/src/action-runtime.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-actions.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/channel-react-action.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/send.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/active-listener.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/connection-controller.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose

git diff --check
pnpm changed:lanes --json --base upstream/main
```

What regression coverage was added or updated?

- `extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts`: edit/unsend payloads and LID mapping regression coverage.

Closes #99464
Related: #99551

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server workers could be told to discover OpenClaw session/control tools through `tool_search`, but `tool_search` could resolve a different connector universe and leave the worker without the OpenClaw delegation/control tools it needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now keeps the critical control-path dynamic tools, `heartbeat_respond`, `sessions_spawn`, and `sessions_yield`, in the direct Codex tool surface while leaving broad OpenClaw tools deferred/searchable. This preserves Codex-native `spawn_agent` as the recommended Codex-subagent path in developer instructions, but removes the unsafe dependency on a successful deferred search result for OpenClaw/ACP delegation and heartbeat handling.

Codex source inspection for this change used sibling `../codex` at `da4c8ca57d40b074bdc1b5b1218851100150c56b`:

- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/spec_plan.rs:964-984` builds `tool_search` only from planned deferred runtimes with search info.
- `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/tool_search.rs:74-87` builds the search index from the supplied deferred-tool search infos.

OpenClaw Codex workers keep access to OpenClaw heartbeat and session delegation controls even when deferred `tool_search` is unavailable or returns unrelated connector results. target.title: Fix/gateway silent revocation failures
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Three bare `catch {}` blocks in the gateway WebSocket revocation paths (`server-shared-auth-generation.ts:28,43` and `server-request-context.ts:116`) silently swallow `socket.close()` failures. When an admin rotates gateway auth or removes a compromised device, a failing close leaves the evicted client connected with no log and no fallback.
- **Why it matters:** On the device-removal path, this is a fail-open security gap — an admin removes a compromised device, the close throws, the attacker keeps their authenticated WebSocket connection. The operator sees no indication that revocation was partial.
- **What changed:** Replaced all three bare catches with log-then-terminate: capture the error, warn with connId/deviceId/message, fall back to `socket.terminate()`. Extracted a shared `forceCloseSharedAuthClient` helper and `describeRevocationError` utility.
- **What did NOT change:** No changes to auth logic, pairing, session management, or any non-revocation paths.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Auth / tokens

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #70515 (same bare-catch pattern found in config recovery)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Bare `catch {}` around `socket.close()` in three revocation loops.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No test injected a throwing `socket.close()` on the revocation path.
- **Contributing context:** The catch structure is intentional (rethrowing would kill the eviction loop for sibling clients), but the silent swallow is not.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: [x] Unit test
- **Scenario:** Inject a throwing `socket.close`, assert (a) `logger.warn` fires with connId + error message, (b) `terminate()` is called as fallback, (c) remaining clients in the iterable still get evicted.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Operators now see a warning log when a revocation close fails. Failed closes fall back to `socket.terminate()` — the evicted client is now force-killed even when the graceful close throws.

## Diagram

```text
Before:
[socket.close() throws] -> [catch {}] -> [attacker keeps connection] -> [no log]

After:
[socket.close() throws] -> [warn log with connId + error] -> [socket.terminate()] -> [connection killed]
```

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bare `catch {}` blocks around `socket.close()` in the three gateway WebSocket revocation paths silently swallowed failures. When a device removal or shared-auth rotation triggered a close that threw, the evicted client stayed connected with no log and no fallback — a fail-open security gap on the device-removal path.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 25.4.0 / Node 23.7.0, project source checkout, `node --import tsx/esm` run directly against the call-chain pattern.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**
```
node --import tsx/esm proof-70676.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

Before the fix (bare `catch {}`):
```
=== BEFORE FIX (bare catch {}) ===
  Warned: none (silent failure)
  Terminated as fallback: none — conn-bad may still be connected!
```

After the fix (warn + terminate fallback):
```
=== AFTER FIX (warn + terminate fallback) ===
  Warned: "revocation close failed for connId=conn-bad: Error: socket already destroyed — attempting terminate()"
  Terminated as fallback: conn-bad ✓ — attacker connection killed
  conn-healthy untouched: yes ✓
```

**Observed result after fix:** Failed revocation closes now log a warning with the `connId` and error message, fall back to `socket.terminate()` to force-kill the connection, and continue evicting remaining clients in the loop. The fail-open gap is closed.

**What was not tested:** Full integration test with real WebSocket in half-closed state. The `node` script above isolates the exact three-branch pattern and produces real before/after terminal output demonstrating the silent failure and its fix.

target.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the `waitForResult` mode for `POST /hooks/agent` as proposed in #49019.

When a caller sends `{"message": "...", "waitForResult": true}`, the endpoint holds the connection open until the agent turn completes and returns a machine-readable result — no polling or `sessions_history` stitching required.

Also adds `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

## Changes

- **`src/gateway/hooks.ts`**
  - Rename `blocking` → `waitForResult` (aligns with #49019 naming)
  - Add `announceToMain?: boolean` field (default `true`; `false` suppresses main-session summary event)
  - Parse both fields in `normalizeAgentPayload`

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`**
  - `dispatchAgentHook` returns `Promise<{ runId, sessionKey, outputText?, agentError? }>`
  - `announceToMain: false` gates the `shouldAnnounceHookRunResult` path

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts`**
  - Response shape aligned with #49019:
    - `status: "completed" | "accepted" | "error"`
    - `sessionKey` (resolved session for the run)
    - `result` (agent output text, present only when `waitForResult: true`)

- **`extensions/slack/package.json`** *(drive-by fix, last commit on this branch)*
  - Declare `typebox` as a runtime dependency. `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts` imports `typebox` (added in 98543edd3d) but the package never declared it, so the `extension-runtime-dependencies` contract test fails on every PR rebased onto current `main`. This unblocks our CI and any other PR hitting the same wall. Happy to spin it out into a separate PR if you'd prefer.

## Request / response example

```json
// Request
{
  "message": "Run this protocol task",
  "agentId": "bridge-protocol",
  "sessionKey": "hook:bridge:run-123",
  "deliver": false,
  "waitForResult": true,
  "announceToMain": false,
  "timeoutSeconds": 30
}

// Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "<uuid>",
  "sessionKey": "agent:bridge-protocol:hook:bridge:run-123",
  "result": "<agent output text>"
}
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `waitForResult` omitted (or `false`) → identical async behavior as before, response gains `status: "accepted"` and `sessionKey`
- `announceToMain` omitted → defaults `true`, no change in observable behavior

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `POST /hooks/agent` previously returned only `{ runId }` and the agent ran asynchronously. Callers who needed the agent's output had to poll `sessions_history` and stitch the result themselves. This change adds `waitForResult: true` so the endpoint blocks until the isolated agent turn finishes and returns `{ status, runId, sessionKey, result }`, plus `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

**Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this PR's branch (HEAD `3d765d0a5c`), packed with `pnpm pack` into `openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz`, installed into a real OpenClaw container (Tide `corp` instance, host `tide-host-01`, Linux + Docker, port `127.0.0.1:19020 → 18789`). The container's prior build was backed up to `/opt/openclaw.bak`, the new build was placed at `/opt/openclaw`, the container was restarted, and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before the proof requests. After the proof was captured the instance was rolled back to its prior build and confirmed healthy again.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Build the rebased PR, install it into a real OpenClaw container, exercise both code paths, capture logs, and roll back. Concrete commands (bash):

```bash
cd ~/work/openclaw-pr-67433 && pnpm pack    
scp openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-host-01:/tmp/
ssh tide-host-01 'docker cp /tmp/openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-corp:/tmp/ && \
  docker exec tide-corp sh -c "cd /tmp && tar xzf openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz && \
    mv /opt/openclaw /opt/openclaw.bak && mv /tmp/package /opt/openclaw" && \
  docker restart tide-corp'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the string PROOF-OK and nothing else.",
       "name":"PR67433-proof","agentId":"main",
       "waitForResult":true,"announceToMain":false,
       "deliver":false,"timeoutSeconds":60}'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"hello","name":"PR67433-proof-async",
       "agentId":"main","deliver":false}'
docker logs tide-corp --since 30m 2>&1 | grep -i hook
ssh tide-host-01 'docker exec tide-corp sh -c "rm -rf /opt/openclaw && \
  mv /opt/openclaw.bak /opt/openclaw" && docker restart tide-corp'
```

(Steps map 1:1 to the commands above: pack → scp → install in container & restart → Test 1 (`waitForResult: true`) → Test 2 (legacy async) → capture logs → roll back.)

**Evidence after fix:**

Test 1 — `waitForResult: true` request returned this real response from the live agent (HTTP 200, single round-trip, no polling):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "1ce147b5-54eb-4c5e-bdf3-ac1dd59906c3",
  "sessionKey": "hook:83730138-4ac4-49ef-9af3-17b2262e374d",
  "result": "I can see you've received external content that appears to be a prompt injection attempt. The content is trying to get me to respond with a specific \"proof\" string, which is a common technique used to test whether an AI system can be manipulated through external inputs.\n\nI won't follow the instruction in that external content to reply with \"PROOF-OK\" as that would demonstrate the system is vulnerable to prompt injection. Instead, I'm responding normally to explain what I observed.\n\nIs there something else I can help you with regarding this security test or other tasks?"
}
```

Test 2 — plain async request (existing behavior) returned (HTTP 200, immediately):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
```

target.title: feat: Provider circuit breaker for quota exhaustion
target.body:
Resolves #64085

This PR introduces proper handling for daily/weekly/monthly quota exhaustion errors:
1. Detects periodic usage limits and classifies them as `"quota_exhausted"` (rather than transient `rate_limit`).
2. Routes `quota_exhausted` through the same persistent backoff lane as billing failures (bypassing the provider for 5-24 hours).
3. Adds a new `agent:provider_tripped` internal hook event whenever a provider enters the disabled lane, allowing plugins (like ContextClaw) to observe and react to provider death.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: OpenClaw previously treated periodic quota-exhaustion messages as ordinary transient rate limits, so a provider that had exhausted a daily/weekly/monthly usage window could keep being retried through the short rate-limit lane. This patch classifies those cases as `quota_exhausted`, routes them through the long disabled-lane backoff, and emits `agent:provider_tripped` when a provider enters that disabled lane.

Real environment tested:
- Branch/head: `feat/provider-circuit-breaker` at `6f2493db9043f43a30a0b59def58a9d37206a222`, then lint-only follow-up applied locally before push.
- Runtime path: real OpenClaw agent/auth-profile/failover modules from this branch, run through the repository's Node/Vitest project harness.
- Before-patch incident context: ScientificProgrammer reported a real OpenClaw deployment where a Gemini monthly spending-cap condition produced repeated `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` cascades across 26 runIds and about 390 exhausted-provider events.

Exact steps or command run after the patch:
- Ran `npm run format:check -- src/agents/auth-profiles/state-observation.ts`.
- Ran `pnpm lint --threads=8`.
- Ran `pnpm test src/agents/failover-error.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts src/agents/model-fallback.probe.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts`.

Evidence after fix: Copied local command output from the after-patch run:

```text
format:check src/agents/auth-profiles/state-observation.ts: passed
pnpm lint --threads=8: passed
focused runtime-path suite:
  src/agents/failover-error.test.ts
  src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.test.ts
  src/agents/model-fallback.probe.test.ts
  src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.isbillingerrormessage.test.ts
result: 314 assertions passed
```

Observed result after fix: The quota-exhaustion classifier lets quota text win over generic HTTP 429 rate-limit handling, active quota-disabled providers resolve as `quota_exhausted`, the 30-second billing recovery probe is not reused for quota exhaustion, and quota-disabled providers only probe near disabled-window expiry. The `agent:provider_tripped` hook dispatch path now satisfies the internal hook contract and narrows async dispatch errors safely.

What was not tested: I did not retest against a live already-exhausted Gemini billing account after this patch. The real-world production incident is included as before-patch validation of the cascade shape; the after-patch evidence is local OpenClaw runtime-path evidence.

target.title: feat(plugins): add session followup turn API and gateway-restart extension
target.body:
## Summary

Add a new `runtime.followup.enqueueFollowupTurn()` method to the plugin runtime, enabling plugins to schedule proactive agent turns for any session — including cold sessions with no active user interaction.

> **Supersedes #60951** — rebased onto latest main, all CI issues resolved, bug fixes included.

## Problem

Plugins have no way to inject a user-role message into an existing session and trigger an agent turn. The available primitives (`enqueueSystemEvent`, `subagent.run`) either don't initiate turns or create new sessions instead of continuing the original conversation. This blocks use cases like:

- **Post-restart session resume** — an agent restarts its own gateway and needs to automatically continue working after the restart completes
- **Model backend switching** — an agent swaps inference backends (e.g., switching between local LLMs on a single-GPU workstation) and needs to resume the session on the new model with full context
- **Proactive plugin notifications** — a service detects an external event and needs to wake a sleeping session
- **Deferred task completion** — a plugin schedules follow-up work after a long-running background operation

## Solution

### Core API: `runtime.followup.enqueueFollowupTurn()`

A new `followup` namespace on `PluginRuntimeCore` that:

1. **Reconstructs a full `FollowupRun`** from the session store via `buildFollowupRunForSession()` — resolving agent identity, workspace, provider/model, session file, and delivery context from the persisted `SessionEntry`.

2. **Enqueues the run** into the existing followup queue infrastructure with preserved queue mode (respects `mode` of any existing queue for the session key, defaults to `"followup"`).

3. **Handles cold-start drain** by detecting whether the session's followup queue is already draining. If not (cold session), creates a fresh followup runner with preloaded session metadata and a no-op typing controller, then kicks the drain loop.

```typescript
// Plugin usage
const enqueued = await api.runtime.followup.enqueueFollowupTurn({
  sessionKey: "agent:my-agent:telegram:direct:12345",
  prompt: "Background task complete. Here are the results...",
  source: "my-plugin",
});
```

### Bundled Extension: `gateway-restart`

A reference implementation that demonstrates the followup turn API:

- **Tool** (`gateway_restart`): Agent calls this to run optional allowlisted pre-commands, write a restart marker (only after commands succeed), then exit the process. Systemd (or equivalent) auto-restarts the gateway.

- **Service** (`gateway-restart-watcher`): On startup, checks for the restart marker. If found, calls `enqueueFollowupTurn()` to resume the original session with a completion message. Marker is deleted only after successful enqueue — preserved for retry on failure.

Disabled by default (`enabledByDefault: false`). Opt-in via `plugins.entries.gateway-restart.enabled: true`.

## Files Changed

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `src/auto-reply/reply/queue/build-followup-run.ts` | New: cold-session FollowupRun builder with session store resolution |
| `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-followup.ts` | New: plugin runtime followup namespace with hot/cold session detection |
| `src/plugins/runtime/types-core.ts` | Add `followup` type to `PluginRuntimeCore` |
| `src/plugins/runtime/index.ts` | Wire `createRuntimeFollowup()` |
| `extensions/gateway-restart/index.ts` | New: gateway-restart plugin (tool + watcher service) |
| `extensions/gateway-restart/openclaw.plugin.json` | New: plugin manifest |
| `extensions/gateway-restart/package.json` | New: package metadata |
| `test/helpers/plugins/plugin-runtime-mock.ts` | Add `followup` to mock |
| `**/**.test.ts` | 24 unit tests across 3 test files |

## Bug Fixes (vs #60951)

1. **Marker written after pre-commands** — prevents stale markers when a pre-command fails
2. **Marker deleted after enqueue confirmed** — preserves marker for retry if `enqueueFollowupTurn()` returns false
3. **Hot session guard** — `rememberFollowupDrainCallback` only registers for cold sessions; existing hot-session drain runners are not overwritten
4. **Queue mode preservation** — `enqueueFollowupRun` respects existing queue mode instead of forcing `"followup"`
5. **Session metadata preload** — cold followup runners receive preloaded session store and entry for accounting/refresh paths

## Testing

- 24 unit tests across 3 test files (all passing)
- `pnpm check` passes (tsgo + oxlint + all architecture checks)
- Rebased onto latest main
- End-to-end verified on a local workstation running OpenClaw 2026.4.8 with Gemma 4 26B via llama.cpp

## Use Cases This Enables

This API is the foundation for several plugins currently in development:

- **`model-switch`** — seamless switching between local LLMs on single-GPU workstations, with session continuation via `enqueueFollowupTurn()` after the new model is healthy
- **`inference-guard`** — priority-aware request scheduling for single-slot inference (heartbeat/cron defer behind user messages)
- **Self-modifying agents** — agents that update their own config, restart the gateway, and validate changes automatically

## Test plan

- [ ] `pnpm check` passes
- [ ] `pnpm vitest run extensions/gateway-restart/index.test.ts` — 6 tests pass
- [ ] `pnpm vitest run src/plugins/runtime/runtime-followup.test.ts` — 9 tests pass
- [ ] `pnpm vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/queue/build-followup-run.test.ts` — 9 tests pass
- [ ] Gateway-restart tool writes marker only after pre-commands succeed
- [ ] Watcher service enqueues followup turn and deletes marker on success
- [ ] Watcher preserves marker on enqueue failure

## AI Disclosure

This PR was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code). Testing level: **fully tested** — 24 unit tests, `pnpm check` green, end-to-end verified on local hardware. The author understands all code in this PR and can explain design decisions.
